en: The Sutra on the Great Cundī Dhāraṇī, the Heart of Seven Koṭis of Buddhas, Spoken by the Buddha;
translated by the Tripitaka Master Śīlabhadra of India during the Great Tang Dynasty.
At that time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
At that moment, the World-Honored One reflected and contemplated out of compassion for all sentient beings of the future.
Having thus spoken this Dharma of the Seven-Crore Buddhas’ Mother Heart Cundī Dhāraṇī,
he then spoke the mantra, saying:
*Namo saptānāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhakoṭīnām | tadyathā | oṃ cale cule cunde svāhā* If there be bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās...
If one upholds, maintains, reads, and recites this dhāraṇī for eight hundred thousand times, all transgressions— including the five crimes of immediate retribution committed over immeasurable kalpas—
will be entirely extinguished.
In whatever place they are born, they shall always encounter all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;
all their requisites shall be fully provided according to their wishes,
and in every birth they shall constantly attain renunciation from the household life.
Fully maintaining the pure precepts of the bodhisattva vows,
they are always reborn among humans and devas and never fall into the evil realms;
they are constantly protected by all the devas.
If there are laymen or laywomen who recite and uphold this,
their households shall not be afflicted by calamities, misfortunes, or the suffering of illness;
whatever they undertake shall meet with success without exception.
The words spoken will be believed and accepted by all people.
If one recites this dhāraṇī mantra one hundred thousand times,
one will see various Buddhas, bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas in dreams.
One will see black objects being spat out from one's own mouth.
If one has grave offenses, by reciting [the mantra] two million times,
one will also see various Buddhas and Bodhisattvas in dreams.
Furthermore, one will see oneself vomiting out black substances;
those who have committed the five heinous crimes shall not obtain such auspicious dreams.
One should further recite it until it reaches seven hundred thousand times.
At that time, one will again obtain signs as previously described,
even to the point of dreaming of vomiting forth white substances such as curd-rice and the like.
One should know that for such a person, their transgressions are extinguished;
this is the mark of purity.
Furthermore, I shall now explain the functions performed by this great dhāraṇī.
If, before an image of the Buddha,
or before a stūpa, or in a pure place,
one smears the ground with cow dung.
Then, construct a square altar according to its required dimensions,
and further offer it flowers, incense, banners, canopies, food, drink, lamps, and candles,
as far as one's means allow.
Furthermore, one should recite mantras over scented water and scatter it in the four directions, above, and below to establish a boundary.
At each of the four corners of the altar and at its center,
one should place a flask of scented water.
The mantra-holder, within the mandala,
kneels with the right knee on the ground facing east and recites the mantra one thousand and eight times.
The incense water flask then turned of its own accord.
He joined his palms, held various flowers,
and recited the mantra one thousand and eight times.
Sprinkle [the water] over a single mirror surface.
Then, facing the mirror directly,
recite the mantra one thousand and eight times.
Upon seeing an image of a Buddha or a Bodhisattva,
one should recite the mantra over flowers one hundred and eight times and scatter them as an offering.
In responding to questions regarding the Dharma, there was nothing he did not resolve with complete clarity.
If there was an illness caused by a ghost, by chanting incantations over *kuśa* grass and brushing it over the patient, they would immediately be healed.
If there were children possessed by ghosts, [the same method applied].
Using threads of five colors, have a young girl twist them into a cord;
recite the mantra once for each knot until twenty-one knots are complete,
and then tie it around her neck.
Recite the mustard-seed mantra seven times and scatter it over the face;
the affliction will immediately be cured.
Furthermore, there is another method.
If one draws the patient's form in ink before them and strikes it with a consecrated willow branch,
the illness shall likewise be cured.
Furthermore, there is another method:
if a sick person is possessed by a spirit and is located at a distance,
one should recite the mantra over willow twigs seven times.
If one entrusts this to another to recite while being struck, the ailment will likewise be cured.
Furthermore, there is a method:
if one recites this mantra while traveling on a road, [the same result shall follow].
There will be no fear of thieves, robbers, wild beasts, or the like.
Furthermore, there is a dharma:
one should constantly maintain this mantra.
In the event of disputes or litigation, there shall be no case where one does not achieve victory.
If one wishes to cross rivers, streams, or the great ocean,
by reciting this mantra while crossing, one will encounter no perils such as predatory beasts within the water.
Furthermore, there are those who are bound,
confined, or have their bodies shackled;
if they recite this mantra, they shall immediately attain liberation.
Furthermore, there is a rite: if in various lands the waters and rains are not regulated and pestilence spreads,
one should mix ghee with sesame and non-glutinous rice.
Take a pinch with three fingers,
recite the mantra once, and place it in the fire to burn;
this may be done for seven days and seven nights.
If one continues in this manner throughout the six periods of the day and night without interruption,
all calamities and epidemics will be completely extinguished.
Furthermore, there is another method.
Upon the sandy banks and shoals of a river,
one uses a seal to imprint the sand into the forms of stupas and images.
Reciting the mantra once forms one stupa.
Upon completing six hundred thousand recitations,
one will either see Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva or [the stupa will appear].
Some may see the Bodhisattva Tārā,
or some may see the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi;
whatever they seek according to their hearts' desire, all shall be fully satisfied.
Or they see themselves being granted elixirs of immortality;
or they see themselves being given and receiving the prediction of enlightenment (*bodhy-avyākaraṇa*).
Furthermore, there is a dharma.
Circumambulate the image of the Bodhi tree to the right and recite the mantra one thousand million times;
you will then see the Bodhisattva preaching the Dharma for you.
If one wishes to follow a bodhisattva, one will immediately be able to accompany them.
Furthermore, there is a dharma:
when begging for alms, one should always maintain this mantra.
One shall not be harmed or afflicted by evil people, malicious dogs, or similar creatures.
If one recites and maintains this mantra three hundred thousand times before a stūpa, an image of the Buddha,
or a śarīra-stūpa, [the aforementioned benefits will be attained].
Furthermore, on the fifteenth day of the waxing moon, one should arrange a great offering and,
without eating for one full day and night,
recite the mantra with right mindfulness until one beholds the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi.
Then that bodhisattva shall take that person to his own palace.
Furthermore, there is a practice:
if one is before a stūpa of the Turning of the Wheel of Dharma, or before a stūpa at the place of the Buddha’s birth.
Or, descending from the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven by means of jeweled stairways before a stūpa or a śarīra-stūpa,
one recites mantras and circumambulates such various stūpas to the right;
thereupon, one will see the Bodhisattva Aparājita and the Bodhisattva Hārītī.
All their wishes were completely fulfilled.
If they required elixirs of the immortals, he would immediately bestow them upon them.
Furthermore, he preached the Dharma for them, showing them the path of the bodhisattva.
If there are those who recite this dhāraṇī,
until they sit at the site of enlightenment,
all bodhisattvas will constantly serve as their virtuous friends.
Furthermore, this Great Dhāraṇī Mahāvidyā-mantra Dharma of Cundā has been taught by all Buddhas of the past and shall be taught by all Buddhas of the future.
All Buddhas of the present are now speaking it;
I too now speak it in this same way for the sake of benefiting all sentient beings.
In order to cause them to attain unsurpassed bodhi,
if there are sentient beings with meager merit who possess no roots of goodness whatsoever.
There is no one lacking the spiritual capacity,
nor anyone lacking the factors of enlightenment, who,
upon hearing this dharani method, [would not attain realization].
One will swiftly realize *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
If there is anyone who can constantly recollect this mantra and maintain it through recitation, [they shall attain this].
Immeasurable roots of goodness were all brought to fulfillment.
When the Buddha preached this Great Cundī Dhāraṇī Dharma,
immeasurable sentient beings distanced themselves from the dust of passion and were freed from defilement.
One shall obtain the merit of the Great Cundī Dhāraṇī Mahāvidyā-mantra;
one shall behold the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and the assembly of all holy ones of the ten directions, pay them homage, and depart.

One fascicle of the *Mahā-saptakoṭi-buddha-mātṛ-hṛdaya-mahā-cundī-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, extracted from the sixty thousand verses of the *Mahā-vidyā-ratna-kośa*, translated at the Xīwèiguó Temple in the second year of the Chuǐgǒng era.
